work_order.approach:
One helper, four callers, no figure changes.

1. The shared rule (IAC-4). Export getEffectiveEndDate(endDate, interval, firstDayOfWeekIdx?) from reportRanges.ts, declared next to validateEnd. Its body is a literal transcription of custom-spreadsheet.ts:120-128: return endDate unchanged unless interval === 'Weekly'; otherwise return currentDay() < getWeekEnd(endDate, firstDayOfWeekIdx) ? today : weekEnd. Carry the canonical comment onto the helper, rewritten to describe the rule rather than a call site. The helper takes the date as an argument because the two families of call site anchor differently (recalculate's non-Weekly branch must receive the report's endDate, not the bucket start).

2. The three existing call sites (IAC-4). custom-spreadsheet.ts:120-128 and grouped-spreadsheet.ts:55-61 become one getEffectiveEndDate call each. recalculate.ts:94-108 collapses to a ternary. Verified safe: _weekRange pushes weekFromDate(end) last (months.ts:299-308), so for the final Weekly bucket getWeekEnd(intervalItem) === getWeekEnd(endDate); and for every non-Weekly interval the helper returns endDate unchanged, exactly what recalculate's else-branch assigns today.

3. The header (IAC-1) — chosen resolution: pass the same clamped value, not new copy. ReportSummary gains an optional firstDayOfWeekIdx prop and renders getEffectiveEndDate(endDate, interval, firstDayOfWeekIdx), including inside the format(startDate) !== format(endDate) collapse check so the separator still collapses correctly. CustomReport.tsx passes the pref it already holds (lines 154-155). Chosen over the copy alternative: no new i18n string, no layout change, and header and buckets stay derived from one function.

4. The budgeted path (IAC-3) — chosen resolution: widen on all paths; no new guard. A word-for-word identical comment sits above the existing balanceTypeOp !== 'totalBudgeted' guard in both factories, recording that the widening applies to every balance type while the week-start remap below does not, because budget rows arrive keyed by month. Verified: fetchBudgetData keys date by month (spreadsheets/budgetDataQuery.ts:231) while Weekly bucket labels are week starts, so no budget row can match a bucket and every Weekly+Budgeted bucket is already 0 today — as is totalBudgeted, which mirrors totalAssets + totalDebts (custom-spreadsheet.ts:350) accumulated from those same buckets. Widening pulls one extra month of rows that are then discarded.

5. Tests (IAC-5). All ten existing weekly cases pass unmodified. Added: ReportSummary.test.tsx pinning the header (one case per interval, with per-interval expected strings — v1's rejected literal, corrected); reportRanges.test.ts pinning the helper with the same discriminating dates; a totalBudgeted weekly case asserting both the widened month list and figure-for-figure equality; a release note.

Scope correction carried from v2: v1's risk list claimed this slice changes the financial figures a user sees, inherited from the issue's Risk paragraph. git log shows the widening landed in b593293 (#12), the commit this issue reviews. The consolidation is value-preserving and the only new behaviour is the header label.
assumptions: getWeekEnd(endDate) equals getWeekEnd(intervalItem) for the final bucket of a Weekly report, because _weekRange pushes weekFromDate(end) last and weekFromDate(end) and end share a week by construction. Verified by reading months.ts:292-311; it holds for any endDate, not just week starts.

fetchBudgetData rows can never match a Weekly bucket, because it keys date by month (spreadsheets/budgetDataQuery.ts:231) while Weekly interval labels are week-start dates. Verified by reading the function; the added test pins the consequence rather than the premise.

Under TestProviders, useDateFormat() returns undefined so ReportSummary's 'MM/dd/yyyy' fallback supplies the day-level format for the Weekly/Daily literals. Verified from prefsSlice's `synced: {}` initial state and the absence of any loadPrefs dispatch in the test setup.

Under TestProviders, t('to') returns the key 'to'. Verified from i18n.ts's fallbackLng: false plus the Balance.test.tsx precedent. If a locale file were ever present and translated, the literals would need the separator built from t('to') rather than hardcoded — but English is the natural-language source here, so it will not move.
work_order.confidence_rationale:
The design is unchanged from v1 and I re-verified every load-bearing claim against the code myself rather than inheriting v2's assertions: the three clamp sites are byte-identical as described; ReportSummary has exactly one importer; custom-spreadsheet.test.ts really does contain exactly ten it( blocks, so IAC-5's 'unchanged' claim is concrete; _weekRange pushes weekFromDate(end) last, which makes recalculate's anchor swap safe; GraphButton does pass title through as aria-label, so the qa_script's selector is real; and the budgeted-path safety argument — the one belief that touches money — confirmed by reading fetchBudgetData's month keying and totalBudgeted's accumulation, so widening provably cannot move a budgeted figure. I also resolved the two environment questions v2 left open: useDateFormat() returns undefined under TestProviders because prefsSlice's initialState.synced is {}, and t('to') returns the key because i18n sets fallbackLng: false, with Balance.test.tsx as the working precedent for untranslated keys under these providers. Both were named unknowns in v2; both are now read off code.

Confidence is above v2's 84 for two reasons: those two unknowns were the main soft spot in the new test file and are now settled, and the scope error that inflated the risk picture is corrected, which materially narrows the blast radius to display-only. It is not in the 90s because ReportSummary.test.tsx has still never been executed by anyone — its rendering path through PrivacyFilter and useFormat is the one thing I reasoned about and could not run — and because this round had no critique to test the plan against, so nothing has survived an adversarial peer pass. One green run of that file plus the month-list assertion would put this in the low 90s.
work_order.debate_summary:
There is no critique to arbitrate this round. plan/critique.json is `{}` — the critic step produced nothing — so what follows is my own verification of the proposal against the code, not a ruling on a disagreement between two agents. That is a real limitation of this round and the main reason confidence is 85 rather than higher: nothing here has survived an adversarial pass from a peer, and a council whose critic is silent is weaker than one whose critic was answered. I say so rather than presenting a tidy verdict.

The three objections recorded against v1 in plan/brief.md were all upheld, and all three were defects in v1's test and QA artifacts rather than in its design. v2 fixes each in place, and I re-verified each fix rather than taking v2's word for it:

(1) The Monthly/Yearly assertion was arithmetically impossible. getIntervalFormat returns the interval's own format — "MMM ''yy" for Monthly, 'yyyy' for Yearly — for anything outside dayLevelIntervals (ReportOptions.ts), so only Daily takes the day-level pref. v1 stated '08/30/2026 to 09/27/2026' for all three intervals. v2 splits the case into three with per-interval expected strings, and strengthens the Yearly case into an exact-textContent assertion of '2026' with no separator — proving the collapse guard still fires now that endDate is a computed value. That is a stronger check than v1's, and it only became available once the impossible literal was removed. Confirmed.

(2) The firstDayOfWeekIdx '1' case could not fail: 2026-09-27 is a Sunday and the terminating Sunday of a Monday-start week, so getWeekEnd('2026-09-27','1') returns the raw To and the clamp is a no-op — the header reads the same whether or not the pref was threaded through. v2 replaces it with the discriminating pair from custom-spreadsheet.test.ts:251: To 2026-09-28 with today pinned to 2026-10-09, asserting 10/04/2026 under '1' and 10/03/2026 under '0'. I re-derived both weekdays independently: 2026-09-28 is a Monday, so under a Monday-start week it ends Sunday 2026-10-04 and under a Sunday-start week it ends Saturday 2026-10-03. Only the pair discriminates; either alone would pass with the wiring removed. The same date discipline is applied to the reportRanges.test.ts cases so the helper test cannot inherit the same no-op. Confirmed.

(3) The qa_script was not performable as written. viewSummary is a local pref defaulting to false, so <ReportSummary> does not render at all until it is enabled, and the block is additionally gated on !isNarrowWidth with the toolbar carrying the toggle gated the same way. v2 adds a step 2 that opens the window and clicks the toggle, and confirms a header is on screen before any reading happens. I checked the selector text rather than trusting it: GraphButton passes title straight through as aria-label and the title is t('Show Summary'). The second half of the objection is also correct — v1's step 4 asked the tester to confirm the summary total changed, but data[balanceTypeOp] was already summed over the widened query, so a correct implementation would have failed a criterion describing a number that never moved. Restated as a date-label check with the reason inline. Confirmed.

One correction I found on my own, in the critic's favour and against the earlier framing: v1's risk list claimed this slice 'changes the financial figures a user sees', inherited from the issue's own Risk paragraph. git log shows the widening landed in b593293 (#12), the commit this issue reviews. The helper consolidation is value-preserving and the only new behaviour is the header label. The blast radius is display-only.

I also corrected one factual error in v2 that no critique raised: its evidence cites budgetDataQuery.ts as living in loot-core/src/server/, which it does not. The file is packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/budgetDataQuery.ts. The argument itself holds — I read the function and the month-keying at line 231 is as described — but a reviewer following the path as written would find nothing.

The brief records no decisions, so no finding could contradict one. I dropped nothing from v1 that the three objections did not already require. The route is correct as assigned (plan → implement → review → qa): review is warranted for a helper extracted into a module several report factories import and for a change to a displayed financial date range, so no route_request is made. v2 correctly drops v1's request to insert plan, which is already on the route.

The dashboard card path (GetCardData.tsx) can still deliver a saved Weekly+Budgeted report un-coerced. The robustness comment now sits at the guard, but nothing prevents such a report from being saved; that combination remains degenerate (every bucket 0) as it is today, and fixing it is not this slice.
risks: ReportSummary.test.tsx has never been executed by anyone. Its environment dependencies are now read off code rather than assumed — useDateFormat() resolving to undefined via prefsSlice's `synced: {}`, and t('to') returning the key via i18n's fallbackLng: false — but they have not been confirmed by a green run. If a literal is wrong in practice the fix is to build the expected string with monthUtils.format, not to change the component.

In recalculate.ts the Weekly anchor changes from the bucket's own start (intervalItem) to the report's endDate. These are the same value for the final Weekly bucket because _weekRange pushes weekFromDate(end) last, and the non-Weekly branch is value-identical because the helper returns endDate unchanged there. This is the highest-risk line in the plan and is covered by the existing 'leaves Daily and Monthly on their existing end bounds' test (custom-spreadsheet.test.ts:266).

Widening the budgeted path is safe only because no month-keyed budget row can match a week-start bucket label, so every Weekly+Budgeted bucket is already 0. If that is ever wrong, widening would change real budgeted figures. The added test asserts the widened month list and figure-for-figure equality so the assumption is checked rather than trusted; if the equality assertion ever fails, the correct move is to switch to the guard branch, not to weaken the assertion.

The Yearly assertion depends on the header node being identifiable so its textContent can be read exactly. If the header turns out to be several nodes, assert on the containing Text element's textContent instead of a substring match over the whole summary.
Adding an optional prop to ReportSummary would be breaking for a future caller. It is optional and the component has exactly one importer today, so this is a non-issue in-tree but recorded.
work_order.root_cause: Two independent causes. (1) The header renders the raw picker value while the spreadsheet factories compute over a wider range — nothing passes the clamped value to the display layer, so the label and the data are derived from two different rules. (2) The clamp is duplicated at three call sites, two of them byte-identical, so the rule can drift between the query bound and the bucket labels. (1) is what a user sees; (2) is why fixing (1) by copy would leave the drift in place.

work_order.understanding: A Weekly custom report names one date range in its header and computes another in its buckets. CustomReport.tsx passes the raw component-state endDate (a week start, since the Weekly From/To pickers only offer week starts) to <ReportSummary>, while the query bound and the final bucket's intervalEndDate are widened to min(today, getWeekEnd(endDate)). With start 2026-08-30, To 2026-09-27, today 2026-10-02, the header reads '08/30/2026 to 09/27/2026' while the final bucket's intervalEndDate is 2026-10-02 — a label that understates by four days what the bucket and the summary total actually cover. The widening itself already shipped in #12 (b593293), so the total is already correct; only the label lags. This slice therefore changes no financial figure: it fixes the header, settles the budgeted-path guard question, and collapses the rule's triplication into one exported helper in reportRanges.ts. All three recorded objections to v1 were upheld and are fixed in v2; each was a defect in v1's test and QA artifacts, not in its design.
unknowns: Whether ReportSummary renders cleanly under TestProviders with no further stubbing — the first run of ReportSummary.test.tsx is the thing to watch. If it fails on a missing provider rather than on an assertion, the fix is a provider stub, not a change to the component.

Whether the header is a single text node or several under jsdom. The Yearly assertion is written against the header Text element's exact textContent, which works either way as long as the node is identifiable; if not, assert on the containing element.
